# Tenancy Requirements Checklist: Database and Multi-Tenancy (Phase 1)

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality of the Phase 1 specification (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, scenario/edge coverage, security posture, assumptions) before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-09-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Review record (2026-09-15)**: Full 30-item review performed against the current spec.md, data-model.md, research.md, plan.md, and master plan §12/§13/§30/§35/§37, after the analyze F1/F2 remediation. Initial result: 25 pass, 5 fail (CHK013, CHK018, CHK022, CHK023, CHK027). All five failures were resolved by reviewer-approved spec amendments the same day (FR-012/SC-004 audit field policy; US2 scenarios 6–9; duplicate-membership edge case) and re-verified: **30/30 pass.**

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are all master plan §12 outcome areas (restaurant model, branch model, users/profiles, staff membership/roles, tables, RLS foundation, database helper functions, audit foundation) each represented by at least one explicit spec requirement? [Completeness, Spec FR-001–FR-005, FR-010, FR-012] — verified: every §12 outcome maps to at least one FR
- [x] CHK002 - Are the defining attributes of each entity specified at requirements level — restaurant public identifier, membership role and optional branch binding, dining-table identity within its branch — without relying on the reader's inference? [Completeness, Spec FR-001, FR-004, FR-005] — verified: FR-001 (public identifier for URLs), FR-004 (one role + branch binding rules), FR-005 + Edge Case ("identifiers are unique per branch"); attribute *types* are correctly plan-level
- [x] CHK003 - Is the complete staff-role set enumerated in the spec (owner, branch manager, cashier, kitchen staff) with the platform super-admin explicitly distinguished from restaurant-scoped staff roles? [Completeness, Spec FR-004, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK004 - Does the spec require tests for every master plan §12 security-test category — cross-restaurant, cross-branch, staff bypass, and direct data-layer access — with none left implicit? [Completeness, Spec FR-011, US2] — verified: FR-011(a)–(d) enumerate all four
- [x] CHK005 - Are the seed-data content requirements specific enough that the isolation demonstration works with zero manual setup (which restaurants, branches, and role-covering memberships must exist)? [Completeness, Spec FR-015, SC-005] — verified: FR-015 names restaurants, branch minimums, role coverage, and carries the "sufficient to demonstrate and test tenant and branch isolation without manual data setup" obligation, which forces the same-restaurant branch pair required by FR-011(b)
- [x] CHK006 - Is the audit record's minimum field set complete per master plan §37 (actor, timestamp, action, resource, change/reason, tenant scope)? [Completeness, Spec FR-012]
- [x] CHK007 - Are the Phase 0 carry-forward requirements restated for the new schema — deterministic zero-rebuild and reproducible type generation? [Completeness, Spec FR-014, FR-016]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 - Is "deterministic ownership path" (FR-006) defined precisely enough to verify — resolvable from the record's own declared relationships, with no ambiguity about what counts as the path? [Clarity, Spec FR-006, US1 scenario 5] — verified: US1 scenario 5 gives the operational definition; data-model concretizes
- [x] CHK009 - Is "deny-by-default access posture" given an operational definition — which access paths, which actor classes, and what outcome count as compliant? [Clarity, Spec FR-008, FR-009] — verified: actor classes (public/unauthenticated/cross-tenant), paths (any; enumerated in FR-009), outcome (denied)
- [x] CHK010 - Are the record classifications "tenant-owned", "branch-scoped", and platform-level (profiles) defined so that every Phase 1 entity can be classified without interpretation? [Clarity, Spec FR-006, FR-008, Key Entities] — verified: each entity's FR states its restaurant/branch binding; Key Entities marks profiles platform-level; data-model states "Platform-level, **not** tenant-owned" explicitly
- [x] CHK011 - Are "uniquely identified within that restaurant" (branch) and "uniquely identifiable within that branch" (dining table) concrete enough to derive an exact uniqueness rule each? [Clarity, Spec FR-002, FR-005, US1 scenarios 2 and 4] — *Resolution 2026-09-15 (analyze F2): FR-002 now states branch display names are NOT uniqueness-constrained in Phase 1 — identity is ID-based via the (restaurant_id, id) anchor; dining-table labels remain unique per branch (FR-005).* Verified in current spec
- [x] CHK012 - Is "append-only" (audit) defined in terms of which operations are permitted and prohibited through which access paths, rather than left as a bare adjective? [Clarity, Spec FR-013, US3] — verified: US3 scenarios 1–4 cover the supported write mechanism, modify/delete denial on every client path, rejection of incomplete writes, and deny-by-default reads
- [x] CHK013 - Is the audit field "change/reason" resolved to a definite policy — one field or two, required or optional — consistent with the incomplete-write rejection behavior? [Clarity, Spec FR-012, Edge Cases] — *Resolved 2026-09-15 (reviewer-approved amendment): FR-012 now states change/reason is a single optional field, with required write-time context = actor, action, resource, and tenant scope; consistent with the Edge Case rejection list and the data-model/contracts implementation.*

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 - Are the three clarified decisions (multi-membership allowed; super-admin modeled only; simulated test identities) applied consistently across FRs, user stories, edge cases, and assumptions, with no residual contradicting text? [Consistency, Spec Clarifications 2026-09-15, FR-004, FR-011, Assumptions] — verified across all five clarification bullets (incl. F1/F2); no contradicting text found
- [x] CHK015 - Is the Phase 1 / Phase 2 boundary (tenant-and-branch scope enforcement now; the per-role permission matrix later) stated identically in the functional requirements, Out of Scope, and Assumptions? [Consistency, Spec FR-009, Out of Scope, Assumptions] — verified: same where-vs-what framing in all three places
- [x] CHK016 - Do the isolation requirements align with Constitution Principles III/IV and master plan §12/§30 without narrowing or widening either authority? [Consistency, Spec FR-008–FR-011] — verified: §30's owner-sees-all-branches semantics preserved in FR-009; role-specific narrowing is the master plan's own §12-vs-§13 phasing, not a widening
- [x] CHK017 - Is branch-scoped staff access to restaurant-scoped data (e.g., may a cashier see the restaurant record or its memberships) either specified or explicitly deferred to Phase 2 — not left ambiguous? [Consistency, Spec FR-009, Out of Scope] — *Resolution 2026-09-15 (analyze F1): FR-009 now explicitly states the Phase 1 reading — restaurant-scoped records readable by all staff of the restaurant; branch-scoped records limited to the assigned branch for branch-scoped roles (owners keep every branch); role-specific narrowing deferred to Phase 2 RBAC.* Verified in current spec
- [x] CHK018 - Do the audit requirements, the incomplete-write edge case, and SC-004 use the same required-field set with no drift between sections? [Consistency, Spec FR-012, FR-013, SC-004, Edge Cases] — *Resolved 2026-09-15 (reviewer-approved amendment): SC-004 now refers to the "full captured-field set" with change/reason marked optional per FR-012, and FR-012 states the captured-vs-supplied distinction; all sections now agree.*

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 - Is each success criterion (SC-001–SC-005) measurable and verifiable without implementation knowledge? [Measurability, Spec SC-001–SC-005]
- [x] CHK020 - Is "equivalent state" in the deterministic-rebuild criterion (SC-002) defined concretely enough that two rebuilds can be compared objectively? [Measurability, Spec SC-002, FR-014] — verified: the comparison basis is objectively assemblable from the artifacts — FR-014 (deterministic recreation from migrations), FR-016 (byte-identical regenerated types on both rebuilds), SC-001 (full suite green on both), and data-model's deterministic fixed-UUID seed; wording gap already recorded as analyze F3 (LOW) and accepted
- [x] CHK021 - Can "100% of tenant-owned entities covered by checks" (SC-003) be evaluated against an enumerable, agreed definition of tenant-owned entities? [Measurability, Spec SC-003, FR-008] — verified: enumerable set (restaurants, branches, staff_memberships, dining_tables, audit_log; profiles platform-level), stated in Key Entities and data-model

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK022 - Do the acceptance scenarios cover both positive (within-scope access granted) and negative (out-of-scope denied) isolation paths for every actor class the seed must provide (owner, branch-scoped staff, multi-restaurant member, modeled super-admin, unauthenticated)? [Coverage, Spec US2, FR-011, FR-015] — *Resolved 2026-09-15 (reviewer-approved amendment): US2 scenarios 6–9 add the positive owner and branch-staff paths, the multi-restaurant member, and the modeled-only super-admin posture; the Independent Test now also covers within-scope reads.*
- [x] CHK023 - Is the multi-membership clarification exercised by at least one acceptance scenario or test requirement (one person holding memberships in two restaurants)? [Coverage, Spec Clarifications 2026-09-15, FR-011, FR-015] — *Resolved 2026-09-15 (reviewer-approved amendment): US2 scenario 8 exercises the multi-restaurant member — exactly the union of two scopes, nothing beyond either.*
- [x] CHK024 - Is the rebuilt-database scenario specified — isolation guarantees holding identically after a zero-rebuild — so determinism and security are tested together, not separately? [Coverage, Spec US2 scenario 5, FR-014]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK025 - Does every declared edge case state a defined expected behavior (a decision), rather than only posing the question? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases] — verified: all 8 answer with a decision (rejected / supported / deferred with owner / denied / reset-restores)
- [x] CHK026 - Is the deferred "restaurant left without an owner" invariant documented as an explicit deferral with its owning feature and rationale, rather than left implicit? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases, Assumptions] — verified: deferral + owning feature (staff-management) + Principle VIII rationale in both Edge Cases and Assumptions
- [x] CHK027 - Are cross-tenant reference attempts and duplicate identifier cases (slug, table label, duplicate membership) specified with rejection semantics? [Edge Case, Spec FR-007, Edge Cases] — *Resolved 2026-09-15 (reviewer-approved amendment): Edge Case added — an identical staff membership (same person, restaurant, role, and branch) is rejected; distinct memberships remain allowed. Matches data-model's `unique nulls not distinct` constraint and tasks T004/T007.*

## Non-Functional / Security Requirements

- [x] CHK028 - Are the security requirements anchored to the trusted data layer for every access path (application, direct data-access API, direct database session), with no reliance on UI-level enforcement? [Security, Spec FR-008, FR-009, Constitution IV]
- [x] CHK029 - Is the simulated-identity testing boundary specified such that tests must exercise real data-layer enforcement (no mocked protection), keeping the acceptance tests honest? [Security, Spec FR-011, Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK030 - Is each of the spec's assumptions either validated by a clarification or explicitly deferred with rationale (multi-membership, simulated identities, customer-role exclusion, audit-event deferral, ownerless-restaurant deferral, shared development database)?
